phdhy0: This week you review the two imperative classes: the **affirmative** (with tú, with usted and, to recognise, with vos) and the **negative**, which uses a different form. Here you practise it in the street: how to get around Guatemala City and how to explain the way to other people.
u0xct5: With tú: the present without the -s
1werkne: To give an instruction to someone you call **tú**, take the tú present and drop the final **-s**: _caminas → camina_, _bebes → bebe_, _subes → sube_. If the verb changes its vowel in the present, the imperative does too: _cierras → cierra_, _vuelves → vuelve_, _pides → pide_.
1u5vifn: Eight very frequent verbs have a short irregular form: **di** (decir), **haz** (hacer), **ve** (ir), **pon** (poner), **sal** (salir), **sé** (ser), **ten** (tener), **ven** (venir).
l57zr6: The imperative sounds kinder with **por favor**, with the person's name or with a reason: _Ana, sube por esta escalera, por favor; es más rápido_.
15elh1g: The eight irregulars fit into one sentence: _Di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven_. Say it aloud like a rhythm.
1t1n3rr: _Vienes_ is present: it describes. To ask, use the irregular imperative: **ven**.
1wnlvvr: With an older person, a customer or someone you don't know, you use **usted**. Start from the **yo** form of the present, drop the **-o** and add the opposite vowel: -ar verbs take **-e** (_camino → camine_); -er and -ir verbs take **-a** (_bebo → beba_, _subo → suba_).
1j6b4u9: Because you start from **yo**, the irregular yo forms carry over to the imperative: _hago → haga_, _pongo → ponga_, _salgo → salga_, _tengo → tenga_, _vengo → venga_, _digo → diga_. Two are special: **ir → vaya** and **ser → sea**.
ytvpgk: For a group (**ustedes**) you add **-n**: _caminen, suban, vayan_. In Spain, with friends, **vosotros** is used (_caminad, subid_), but you only need to recognise it.
13m0swv: With **usted** the vowel changes: pas**e**. _Pasa_ is for tú.
1iibo51: Start from _yo vengo_: **venga**, with no i.
b4exlj: In Guatemala, in other Central American countries, in Argentina and in Uruguay many people say **vos** instead of tú. It is a correct, normal form; you don't need to use it, but it's useful to recognise it.
17bmwx3: The vos imperative looks like the infinitive without the **-r**, stressed at the end: _caminá, comé, subí_. The vowel doesn't change: _cerrá, volvé, pedí_. It has almost no irregulars: _vení, decí, hacé, poné, salí_. For **ir** people say **andá**.
vcwxnm: If someone says _Vení, sentate_ to you, understand _Ven, siéntate_.
1dxcb5v: The same instruction, three forms of address
2t19y7: To say what someone should **not** do, it isn't enough to put _no_ in front of the affirmative. The negative uses the opposite vowel, like usted, plus the **-s** of tú: _cruza → no cruces_, _bebe → no bebas_, _sube → no subas_.
2zxtva: It also starts from the **yo** form: _hago → no hagas_, _salgo → no salgas_, _digo → no digas_, _tengo → no tengas_. And again two are special: **no vayas** (ir) and **no seas** (ser). With **usted**, the negative is the same as the affirmative with _no_: _no cruce, no vaya_.
10popnk: Watch the spelling, to keep the sound: _llegar → no llegues_, _buscar → no busques_, _cruzar → no cruces_. A reason next to it softens the prohibition: _No pagues en efectivo: con la tarjeta es más barato_.
14yrspx: Trick: the negative tú form is the usted form + **s**: _no cruce → no cruces_, _no vaya → no vayas_.
1gmkpd8: The negative changes the vowel: no to**ques** (c → qu).

h8bvcq: Tú, vos or usted? The stress of the word
2ygzze: With **tú**, the imperative is stressed on the second-to-last syllable: _es-PE-ra, CRU-za, SI-gue_.
hygpyr: With **vos**, the stress jumps to the **end**, so it has a written accent: _es-pe-RÁ, cru-ZÁ, se-GUÍ_. This is the clearest clue to recognise it.
17yza9z: With **usted**, the stress is in the same place as with tú, but the **last vowel** changes: _CRU-ce, SI-ga, es-PE-re_. Listen carefully to the ending.
dsfnsz: To keep the sound in the negative and with usted: **c → qu** (_busque, no busques_), **g → gu** (_llegue, no llegues_), **z → c** (_cruce, no cruces_).
152hegu: Same stress, CRU-; only the last vowel changes.
